methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create a shared vault in an organization.

 The vault belongs to the organization and starts empty. It starts
 private, so only the organization's admins may use it until it is
 shared, unless it is created with organization visibility
 (metadata.visibility), which shares it with every member at once.

methods.name: Update
methods.description:
Update a vault's name, description and external id.

 Entries are kept as stored: change them with setSecrets, removeSecrets,
 setConnection and removeConnections.

methods.name: UpdateVisibility
methods.description:
Update the visibility of a shared vault.

 Setting org lets every member of the organization use the vault in
 their runs. My vault is always private.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete a vault and every value it holds.

 Sessions, schedules, shares, channels and platform clients that name the
 vault are refused at their next run, naming it.

methods.name: SetSecrets
methods.description:
Save secrets in a vault, replacing any saved under the same names.

 Naming the caller's own My vault creates it on its first write.

methods.name: RemoveSecrets
methods.description: Remove secrets from a vault by name.

methods.name: SetConnection
methods.description:
Save a login in a vault at the address of the tool or Git host it is
 for, replacing any saved at the same address.

 Naming the caller's own My vault creates it on its first write.

methods.name: RemoveConnections
methods.description: Remove logins from a vault by address.

methods.name: StartSignIn
methods.description:
Start a sign-in at an address, to save the login in a vault.

 Answers the login page to send the person to. When they have signed in,
 the page they return to calls completeSignIn with what the login page
 handed back. The sign-in must be completed within ten minutes.

 The login fills every HTTP tool whose URL is the address, and a Git
 host's login serves clones from that host.

methods.name: CompleteSignIn
methods.description:
Finish a sign-in: exchange the code the login page handed back and save
 the login in the vault the sign-in was started for, replacing any login
 saved at the address.

 Only the person who started the sign-in may finish it.

methods.name: CreateConnectLink
methods.description:
Make a Connect link: a one-time page where someone without a Stigmer
 account signs in at an address, and the login is saved into a shared
 vault.

 An integrator makes one for each customer's vault and sends the
 customer to its url. The customer sees one Stigmer page with a
 Continue button, then the login page, then returns to return_url.

 Refused for My vault, and for an address nothing can sign in to (no
 login app for it and, for a tool's URL, no login server it advertises).

methods.name: GetConnectLink
methods.description: What a Connect link is for, to show before the customer continues.

methods.name: StartConnectLink
methods.description:
Start the sign-in a Connect link is for. Answers the login page to send
 the customer to; it returns them to the console's callback page.

methods.name: CompleteConnectLink
methods.description:
Finish a Connect link's sign-in and spend the link. Answers where to
 send the customer: the link's return URL with stigmer_connect=connected,
 or stigmer_connect=error and a short reason when the sign-in failed
 after the login page (the link then stays usable until it expires).

methods.name: GetByReference
methods.description: Get a vault by its organization-scoped reference (org/slug).

methods.name: GetMine
methods.description:
Get the caller's own My vault in an organization.

 Answers NOT_FOUND until the caller saves their first login or secret.

methods.name: GetByExternalId
methods.description: Get a shared vault by the integrator's own id for it.

methods.name: List
methods.description:
List the vaults the caller can see in an organization: their own My
 vault and the shared vaults they may view.

methodTypes.name: UpdateVisibilityInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for updating the visibility of any API resource.

 Used by resource-specific command controllers to change visibility.
 Each controller's updateVisibility RPC accepts this shared input
 and returns the full updated resource.

 Visibility transitions trigger FGA tuple management in Cloud mode. Each
 level maps to exactly one tuple shape; on a transition the tuple for the
 old level is removed and the tuple for the new level is created:
 - PRIVATE:  no visibility tuple (owner + explicit grants only)
 - ORG:      resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

 Not all resources support all visibility levels — the supported set is
 declared per kind via VisibilityConfig in kind_meta:
 - Blueprints (agent, skill, mcp_server, plugin):
     PRIVATE, ORG, or CHILD_ORGS
 - Org-only kinds (vault):
     PRIVATE or ORG (never CHILD_ORGS — tenant isolation)

 visibility_public is refused for every kind (INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the
 supported levels); the level is retired.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: ID of the resource whose visibility is being updated.

fields.name: Visibility
fields.description:
The new visibility setting for the resource.
 Must not be unspecified (0). Valid values depend on resource kind —
 see the VisibilityConfig in the kind's kind_meta.

methodTypes.name: SetVaultSecretsInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for saving secrets in a vault. Secrets already saved under other
 names are kept.

fields.name: Vault
fields.description: The vault to save into.

fields.name: Secrets
fields.description: Secrets by name. A name that is already saved has its value replaced.

methodTypes.name: RemoveVaultSecretsInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for removing secrets from a vault by name. Names that are not saved
 are ignored.

fields.name: Vault
fields.description: The vault to remove from.

fields.name: Names
fields.description: Names of the secrets to remove.

methodTypes.name: SetVaultConnectionInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for saving a login in a vault, at the address of the tool or Git
 host it is for.

fields.name: Vault
fields.description: The vault to save into.

fields.name: Address
fields.description:
The address the login is for: a tool's URL (https://mcp.example.com/mcp)
 or a Git host (github.com).

 A tool's address keeps its scheme, host, port and path; the server
 lowercases the scheme and host, drops a default port and one trailing
 slash, and drops any query or fragment. A Git host is its bare host name.

fields.name: Token
fields.description: The access token.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: What the login is for. Empty keeps the description already saved.

methodTypes.name: RemoveVaultConnectionsInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for removing logins from a vault by address. Addresses that are not
 saved are ignored.

fields.name: Vault
fields.description: The vault to remove from.

fields.name: Addresses
fields.description: Addresses of the logins to remove, in any shape setConnection accepts.

methodTypes.name: StartSignInInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for starting a sign-in at an address. The login is saved into the
 named vault when the sign-in completes.

fields.name: Vault
fields.description:
The vault the login is saved into: a shared vault the caller may edit,
 or the caller's own My vault.

fields.name: Address
fields.description:
The address to sign in to: a tool's URL (Linear's MCP endpoint at
 mcp.linear.app/mcp, over https) or a Git host (github.com), in any shape
 setConnection accepts.

fields.name: ReturnTo
fields.description: Where the login page sends the person back to. Unset means web.

fields.name: LoopbackPort
fields.description:
The port of the desktop app's page, for return_to loopback only: one of
 the three Stigmer Desktop listens on (17237 to 17239). A login server
 registers Stigmer once per return address, so the ports are few.

methodTypes.name: StartSignInOutput
methodTypes.description: The login page to send the person to.

fields.name: AuthorizationUrl
fields.description: The login page, with every parameter the sign-in needs.

fields.name: State
fields.description:
The value the login page hands back with the code; completeSignIn takes
 it.

fields.name: ProviderName
fields.description:
Who the person signs in with, for display ("GitHub", or the address's
 host when the login server has no name).

fields.name: Scopes
fields.description: The permissions asked for.

methodTypes.name: CompleteSignInInput
methodTypes.description: Input for finishing a sign-in, with what the login page handed back.

fields.name: State
fields.description: The state from startSignIn, as the login page returned it.

fields.name: Code
fields.description: The authorization code the login page returned.

methodTypes.name: CompleteSignInOutput
methodTypes.description: The login a sign-in saved.

fields.name: Address
fields.description: The address the login was saved at.

fields.name: Description
fields.description:
How the saved login is described: the account when the login app says
 who signed in ("GitHub @ana"), else the host ("Signed in at
 mcp.linear.app").

methodTypes.name: CreateConnectLinkInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for making a Connect link: a one-time page an integrator sends its
 customer, where the customer signs in at an address and the login is saved
 into the integrator's vault for that customer. The customer needs no
 Stigmer account.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization the vault belongs to, by slug or id.

fields.name: VaultId
fields.description:
The shared vault the login is saved into, by id. My vault is refused:
 a link is for someone else.

fields.name: Address
fields.description: The address the customer signs in to: a tool's URL or a Git host.

fields.name: ReturnUrl
fields.description:
Where the customer is sent once the sign-in is over: an absolute https
 URL (http only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]), with no user name or
 password in it. Stigmer adds stigmer_connect=connected, or
 stigmer_connect=error with a short reason.

fields.name: ExpiresInSeconds
fields.description:
How long the link stays usable, in seconds: 60 to 86400 (a day).
 Unset means 1800 (30 minutes).

methodTypes.name: ConnectLink
methodTypes.description:
A Connect link. It works once: the first sign-in saved through it spends
 it.

fields.name: Url
fields.description:
The page to send the customer to. It carries the link's secret: send it
 only to that customer.

fields.name: ExpiresAt
fields.description: When the link stops working.

methodTypes.name: ConnectLinkTokenInput
methodTypes.description: A Connect link's secret, as its url carries it.

fields.name: Token
fields.description: The secret from the link's url.

methodTypes.name: ConnectLinkInfo
methodTypes.description: What a Connect link is for.

fields.name: ProviderName
fields.description: Who the customer signs in with ("GitHub", or the address's host).

fields.name: Address
fields.description: The address the customer signs in to.

fields.name: OrganizationName
fields.description: The name of the organization the login is saved for.

methodTypes.name: StartConnectLinkOutput
methodTypes.description: The login page a Connect link's sign-in starts at.

fields.name: AuthorizationUrl
fields.description: The login page, with every parameter the sign-in needs.

fields.name: State
fields.description: The value the login page hands back with the code.

methodTypes.name: CompleteConnectLinkInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for finishing a Connect link's sign-in, with what the login page
 handed back.

fields.name: Token
fields.description: The secret from the link's url.

fields.name: State
fields.description: The state the login page returned.

fields.name: Code
fields.description:
The authorization code the login page returned; empty when it returned
 an error instead.

fields.name: Error
fields.description:
The error the login page returned instead of a code (RFC 6749 section
 4.1.2.1), such as access_denied when the customer declined.

methodTypes.name: CompleteConnectLinkOutput
methodTypes.description: Where to send the customer once a Connect link's sign-in is over.

fields.name: ReturnUrl
fields.description:
The link's return URL, with stigmer_connect=connected, or
 stigmer_connect=error and a reason: denied (the customer declined),
 provider_error (the login page refused), expired (the sign-in took longer
 than ten minutes), failed (the login could not be saved) or not_allowed
 (the link's maker may no longer change the vault).

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource by org and slug.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Vault, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical format: "org/slug" (e.g., "acme/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

 Every reference in a resource's spec is checked when the resource is
 written: the target must exist, and a target in another organization
 must be one the writing organization's parent shares with its child
 organizations (visibility_child_orgs) to be referenced at all. A blueprint may not be
 more visible than the skills, MCP servers and agents it references, so
 what a person can run they can also read. A reference that fails the
 check is refused at write, never at run.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource, by slug or id.

 When non-empty: an organization slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 2-63 characters; e.g. "stigmer", "acme-corp") or an
 organization id (org_<ulid>). The server stores the id, so a stored
 reference keeps pointing at its organization across a rename.

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form, the id).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 An explicit other org is accepted only when that organization is your
 organization's parent and shares the resource with its children
 (visibility_child_orgs).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, MCP_SERVER).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter
 and end with a letter or digit (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 2-63 characters.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
Version of the resource (optional, only applicable to versioned resources like Skills).
 Supports three formats:
 1. Empty/unset → Resolves to "latest" (most recent version)
 2. Tag name → Resolves to version with this tag (e.g., "stable", "v1.0")
 3. Exact hash → Immutable reference to specific version (e.g., "abc123...")

 Default behavior: Empty means "latest" (current version).
 This field is ignored for non-versioned resources.

 Examples:
 - version: ""           → Use latest version
 - version: "latest"     → Use latest version (explicit)
 - version: "stable"     → Use version tagged as "stable"
 - version: "v1.0"       → Use version tagged as "v1.0"
 - version: "abc123..."  → Use exact version with this hash (immutable)

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)
 - PUBLIC: retired; see the value's own comment.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, agent_share,
 skill, mcp_server), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Retired. This level made a resource readable to every account on the
 server; it is refused at create and at updateVisibility for every kind,
 and every stored row that held it has been moved to visibility_org.
 Sharing across organizations happens through plugins (a copy is
 installed and owned) or, from a parent organization to its children,
 through visibility_child_orgs.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role SSO auto-provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (The tuple once targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; the authorization model no longer admits
 that shape.)

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

enumTypes.name: SignInReturn
enumTypes.description:
SignInReturn says where the login page sends the person back to once they
 have signed in. The server builds the address from this choice; a caller
 never writes it.

values.name: web
values.description: The console's callback page on this deployment.

values.name: desktop
values.description:
The console's callback page, which hands the result on to the desktop
 app (the page opens the app's own link).

values.name: loopback
values.description:
A page the desktop app serves on this machine: the path
 /auth/oauth/callback over plain http on 127.0.0.1 at loopback_port
 (RFC 8252 section 7.3, for apps on the person's own computer).

values.name: api_resource_version
values.description: Immutable version record tracking changes to an API resource.

values.name: iam_policy
values.description: Role-based access control policy for granting permissions on resources.

values.name: identity_account
values.description: User account in the identity system.

values.name: api_key
values.description: Credential for programmatic API access.

values.name: invitation
values.description: Shareable link for joining an organization with a configurable role.

values.name: identity_provider
values.description: External identity provider for federated authentication.

values.name: oauth_app
values.description: Registered OAuth application with an external vendor for outbound authentication.

values.name: platform_client
values.description: OAuth2 client credential for platform builders embedding Stigmer into their products.

values.name: team
values.description: Named group of an organization's people that access is shared with as one.

values.name: organization
values.description:
The boundary that holds people, Agents, Sessions and secrets
 together; nothing outside it sees them.

 Its id is a minted org_<ulid> that never changes; every organization-scoped
 resource names it by that id (metadata.org). Its slug is unique across the
 server and may change through rename; requests may name the organization
 by either.

values.name: platform
values.description: Singleton platform instance representing the Stigmer deployment.

values.name: agent
values.description: AI assistant with instructions, tools, skills, and a delegation model.

values.name: run
values.description: Single run of an agent within a session, tracking tool calls and responses.

values.name: session
values.description: Conversation thread between a user and an agent.

values.name: skill
values.description: Knowledge resource that provides domain-specific context to an agent.

values.name: mcp_server
values.description: External tool server connected via the Model Context Protocol.

values.name: agent_share
values.description: Hosted chat link for an agent with its own audience, origins, and credentials.

values.name: agent_channel
values.description: Connection binding an agent to an external messaging platform workspace.

values.name: channel_app
values.description:
Customer-owned messaging-platform app (e.g. a Slack app) that agent
 channels can install through instead of the shared platform app.

values.name: execution_context
values.description: User-owned runtime context for managing execution state.

values.name: schedule
values.description: Recurring trigger that runs an agent on a cron schedule.

values.name: memory
values.description: Agent-proposed, user-confirmed fact the platform remembers about a person.

values.name: plugin
values.description:
An installed Agent Plugins package: the archive Stigmer materialised into
 skills, MCP servers and an agent, and the handle that upgrades
 and removes them together. A plugin is what you install; an agent is what
 runs. Members are the resources labelled with the plugin's id.

values.name: vault
values.description:
A person's or an organization's box of logins (matched by a tool's
 address) and secrets (matched by name) that runs use.

values.name: plan
values.description:
Catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that buy it.

 Platform-level: a plan belongs to no organization, so it carries no
 authorization scope and no owner. Immutable once created; a change of
 terms is a new Plan and the old one retires.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
An organization's binding to a Plan; at most one active per organization.

 System-created: the payment system drives its lifecycle, so it has no
 owner and grants no roles. Its reads and writes authorize on the
 organization through the billing permissions.

values.name: license
values.description:
A signed grant of entitlements to a self-hosting customer for a term.

 Platform-level: issued by the cloud's operators and verified offline by
 the Enterprise server, so the customer is a value inside the license
 (which may or may not name a cloud organization) and the kind has no
 authorization scope and no owner. Claims are immutable once signed; a
 renewal is a new License.

resourceDescription:
Vault holds the logins and secrets that runs use: connections matched by a
 tool's address, and secrets matched by name.

 A person's own vault, My vault, is created the first time they save a login
 or a secret, and serves their own chats. A shared vault belongs to the
 organization: an admin creates it and says who may use it. Saved values can
 be replaced but are never returned by any read.
